topic: Does ECG acquisition context, rather than the waveform, carry the reported prognostic discrimination of ED ECG deep learning?

sources.title: Biases in electronic health record data due to processes within the healthcare system: retrospective observational study
sources.notes: Correction published as BMJ 2018;363:k4416. Key numbers used: order presence associated with survival odds in 233 of 272 tests; order timing more predictive than result in 118 of 174 tests.
sources.what_it_did: Showed that the presence and the timing of a laboratory order predict survival, in 233 of 272 test types, and that timing beat the result itself for 118 of 174 tests
sources.comparator: Not applicable; the process variables are the exposure
sources.bearing: Supports. The premise of this audit, one modality removed

sources.title: Informative presence and observation in routine health data: A review of methodology for clinical risk prediction
sources.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
sources.what_it_did: Reviewed informative presence and informative observation as a methodological problem for clinical risk prediction
sources.comparator: None; a review of methods
sources.bearing: Supports, and bounds. Establishes the phenomenon and shows the treatment is entirely tabular

sources.title: Informative presence bias in analyses of electronic health records-derived data: a cautionary note
sources.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
sources.what_it_did: Simulated how informative presence propagates into biased estimates across realistic utilisation patterns
sources.comparator: None; a simulation study
sources.bearing: Supports. Gives the bias structure this audit assumes

sources.title: On the nature of informative presence bias in analyses of electronic health records
sources.notes: 33(1):105-113. Adjusting for visit count does not fully remove the bias.
sources.what_it_did: Characterised informative presence as a misclassification bias arising more widely than assumed, and showed adjusting for visit counts does not remove it
sources.comparator: None; an analytic treatment
sources.bearing: Supports, and complicates. The obvious correction is itself unsafe

sources.title: Shortcut learning in medical AI hinders generalization: method for estimating AI model generalization without external data
sources.notes: 7:124. 13 datasets including ECG; performance overestimated by up to 20 percent on average due to data acquisition bias. No metadata-only arm.
sources.what_it_did: Estimated performance overstatement from acquisition-linked shortcuts across 13 datasets by disrupting spatio-temporal structure so that only acquisition-linked information survives
sources.setting: X-ray, CT, ECG, discharge summaries, lung sound
sources.comparator: None. The probe perturbs the signal rather than replacing it with metadata
sources.bearing: Supports, and is the nearest method. It asks whether the model uses acquisition artefacts in the signal, not whether the decision to record predicts the outcome

sources.title: Phenotypic selectivity of artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography in cardiovascular diagnosis and risk prediction
sources.notes: 152(18):1282-1294. Competing explanation for non-specificity: shared pathophysiology. Correlation of phenotype association patterns 0.67 to 0.96.
sources.what_it_did: Found that image-based AI-ECG models built for distinct cardiovascular conditions produce highly correlated phenotype associations, and attributed this to shared pathophysiology
sources.comparator: None; no metadata arm
sources.bearing: Challenges, and is the competing explanation for the non-specificity this audit set out to explain. Our matched arm turned out to favour it over ours.

sources.title: Towards artificial intelligence-based learning health system for population-level mortality prediction using electrocardiograms
sources.notes: 6:21. Source of the horizon-collapse figures: age and sex baseline 0.680 / 0.716 / 0.776 at 30 days / 1 year / 5 years; ECG traces alone 0.843 / 0.812 / 0.798. Alberta cohort, not MDS-ED.
sources.what_it_did: Reported an age-and-sex baseline against a residual network on ECG traces at three mortality horizons in a linked population cohort
sources.comparator: Yes: age and sex, at every horizon
sources.bearing: Supports, as imported motivation only. The waveform margin over demographics narrows as the horizon lengthens, a pattern the paper does not name

sources.title: Enhancing clinical decision support with physiological waveforms — A multimodal benchmark in emergency care
sources.notes: 192(Pt A):110196. PMID 40311469. Upgraded at this stage from arXiv:2407.17856, which is now superseded: the version of record exists and the protocol cites it. Three differences from the preprint matter. The published title is not the preprint's and shares no phrase with it: the MDS-ED acronym is gone and so is the dataset framing, which is why carrying the arXiv title beside this DOI named a paper that does not exist. Corrected at this stage against Crossref; the label count is 1,428 diagnostic labels plus 15 deterioration targets rather than the 1,443 the preprint reported; and the first author's family name is the compound Lopez Alcaraz, which both Crossref and PubMed index under Alcaraz alone. That is how this entry and the dataset entry came to render one person two ways; both now use the author's own form. The audited artifact is still the PhysioNet release [mdsed_physionet], not this paper.
sources.what_it_did: Assembled the modalities available in the first 90 minutes of an emergency-department stay and published 15 deterioration labels with baselines
sources.setting: 12-lead ECG plus tabular, MIMIC-IV emergency department
sources.comparator: Yes: demographics, biometrics, and vitals with laboratory values. No acquisition-context arm
sources.bearing: The audit target's describing paper

sources.title: MIMIC-IV-Ext-MDS-ED: Multimodal Decision Support in the Emergency Department, a Benchmark Dataset for Diagnoses and Deterioration Prediction in Emergency Medicine, version 1.0.0
sources.notes: Restricted access: signed DUA plus CITI Data or Specimens Only Research. 1428 ICD-10 codes, 15 deterioration labels, ICU admission at two horizons, mortality at seven horizons.
sources.what_it_did: Released the credentialed benchmark: cohort, published split, labels and tabular arm
sources.comparator: Not applicable; a data record
sources.bearing: The audited artifact itself

sources.title: Deep survival analysis from adult and pediatric electrocardiograms: a multi-center benchmark study
sources.verify_method: crossref DOI resolution and, independently, the Europe PMC core record for the same DOI (PMID 41408648, PMC12821881); title, all six authors, venue and the 2025-12-17 issue date agree across both
sources.notes: VERSION OF RECORD, substituted for the arXiv preprint on 2026-09-03 after the corresponding check --upgrade-preprints found the published version. The preprint carried an earlier title, 'Benchmarking mortality risk prediction from electrocardiograms'. The two figures this project quotes were re-read against the published abstract and are unchanged: median concordance Code-15 0.83, MIMIC-IV 0.78, BCH 0.81, so the range 0.78 to 0.83 quoted in related work still holds and now holds of a peer-reviewed source. MIMIC-IV, Code-15, BCH. Demographic-only and gradient boosting baselines; no acquisition-context arm. Code at github.com/cavalab/ecg-survival-benchmark.
sources.what_it_did: Benchmarked deep survival and horizon-classification approaches for all-cause mortality against demographic-only and gradient-boosting baselines across three cohorts, and reported that demographic-only models sometimes outperformed externally trained AI-ECG models
sources.setting: 12-lead ECG, MIMIC-IV, Code-15, a paediatric cohort
sources.comparator: Yes: demographics and tabular boosting. No acquisition-context arm
sources.bearing: Supports, and is the closest existing ally. It takes baselines seriously and its own demographic arm sometimes wins

sources.title: Decision curve analysis: a novel method for evaluating prediction models
sources.notes: 26(6):565-574. Method for the net-benefit secondary analyses.
sources.what_it_did: Introduced decision curve analysis, evaluating a model by its consequences at a decision threshold rather than by discrimination
sources.comparator: Treat-all and treat-none as reference strategies
sources.bearing: Adopted. The clinical-utility analysis follows it

sources.title: Deep learning predicts hip fracture using confounding patient and healthcare variables
sources.notes: 2:31. PMID 31304378; full text read at PMC6550136. The hospital-process feature set is enumerated there as order date and day of week, order priority, technician, radiologist, radiation dose, order-to-acquisition time, and two interpretation intervals.
sources.what_it_did: Fit a hospital-process-only arm with no image data and found it beat the image arm, with the image adding nothing when combined
sources.setting: Pelvic radiographs, hip fracture, one health system
sources.comparator: Yes, and it is the arm this audit proposes: process-only, no signal. It won
sources.bearing: Challenges the novelty claim and supports the recommendation. The nearest prior work by a wide margin; its target is diagnosis of a finding visible in the image rather than downstream prognosis, and it registered no numeric target

sources.title: Leveraging large scale deep learning models for diagnosis and visual outcome prediction in retinitis pigmentosa
sources.notes: 9(1):137. PMID 41507439; full text read at PMC12887015. The metadata are age, sex, laterality, cataract presence and cataract surgery history.
sources.what_it_did: Ran an image-only, a metadata-only and a hybrid arm against a time-to-event visual-outcome target, and named the metadata-only arm as such
sources.setting: Fundus photographs, retinitis pigmentosa, survival target
sources.comparator: Yes: a metadata-only Cox baseline, near chance
sources.bearing: Complicates the novelty claim on terminology. A metadata-only prognostic arm by that name is already in print; its metadata are demographic and clinical, with no acquisition-process variable

sources.title: Variable generalization performance of a deep learning model to detect pneumonia in chest radiographs: A cross-sectional study
sources.notes: 15(11):e1002683. PMID 30399157. Hospital system recovered from 99.95 percent of one site's radiographs; sorting by site alone reached AUC 0.861 on the joint dataset.
sources.what_it_did: Showed a pneumonia classifier generalised unevenly across three sites, that site identity was recoverable from almost every radiograph, and that sorting by site alone discriminated well
sources.comparator: Yes, implicitly: site identity alone, a non-physiological variable
sources.bearing: Supports, and supplies the cleanest analogue. A variable indexing where and under what case mix the test was ordered discriminates on its own

sources.title: The impact of site-specific digital histology signatures on deep learning model accuracy and bias
sources.notes: 12(1):4423. PMID 34285218; full text read at PMC8292530. Site was recoverable from the slide at near ceiling, and under preserved-site cross-validation a fifth of previously detectable features were no longer detectable.
sources.what_it_did: Showed that site-specific digital histology signatures are recoverable at near-ceiling accuracy and that progression-free-survival predictions were substantially driven by them
sources.setting: Whole-slide histology, six cancer subtypes, TCGA
sources.comparator: Yes: a clinical-characteristics-only arm predicting site, far weaker than the image
sources.bearing: Supports, and is the best non-ECG prognostic precedent. Prognostic claims specifically weakened once the acquisition signature was controlled

sources.title: Identifying Biases in a Multicenter MRI Database for Parkinson's Disease Classification: Is the Disease Classifier a Secret Site Classifier?
sources.venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.notes: 28(4):2047-2054. PMID 38198251. Freezing the disease model and retraining only the final layer read off sex, scanner type and site at accuracies comparable to the disease task itself.
sources.what_it_did: Froze a trained disease classifier and retrained only its final layer to show that acquisition identity is linearly decodable from the task model's own representation
sources.comparator: None. A probe of the signal model rather than a separate arm
sources.bearing: Supports, and supplies the natural robustness check for this design. Acquisition identity can be internalised by the signal model even when a metadata arm fails.

sources.title: AI for radiographic COVID-19 detection selects shortcuts over signal
sources.notes: 3:610-619. The bibliographic record is Crossref-verified. The version of record could not be fetched in-session, so the descriptive wording was read from the medRxiv preprint of the same title and no numeric result is attributed to this source.
sources.what_it_did: Showed published COVID-19 radiograph classifiers rely on confounders rather than pathology, and that evaluating on external data does not by itself establish that a model reads medically relevant signal
sources.comparator: None; an explainability analysis
sources.bearing: Supports, and answers the external-validation objection. If external validation cannot certify that discrimination comes from physiology, a dedicated acquisition-context arm is not a redundant extra

sources.title: AI recognition of patient race in medical imaging: a modelling study
sources.notes: 4(6):e406-e414. PMID 35568690. Race was predicted across modalities at high discrimination while the hypothesised physiological mediators performed near chance, and the ability survived across anatomical regions and frequency bands.
sources.what_it_did: Showed deep models recover self-reported race from medical images at high discrimination, robustly, while the plausible physiological proxies do not
sources.comparator: Yes: body-mass index, disease distribution and breast density, all near chance
sources.bearing: Bounds the null reported here. Ruling out obvious mediators is not ruling out the pathway, and a failed metadata arm does not license the conclusion that the model reads physiology

sources.title: Shortcut learning in deep neural networks
sources.notes: 2:665-673. The DOI suffix is -00257-z. A plausible variant ending -00257-6 does not resolve, and was rejected in-session rather than written down.
sources.what_it_did: Unified many reported deep-learning failures as one phenomenon, decision rules that perform well on a benchmark and fail under more demanding testing, and argued the remedy lies in how models are benchmarked and reported
sources.comparator: Not applicable; a perspective
sources.bearing: Supports at the level of concept and vocabulary, and its recommendation stance is the paper's own: address shortcuts through reporting, not only through training

sources.title: Imputation and missing indicators for handling missing data in the development and deployment of clinical prediction models: A simulation study
sources.notes: 32(8):1461-1477. The same first author as [sisk2021], later testing rather than reviewing: missingness indicators help in many cases but can be harmful under outcome-dependent missingness.
sources.what_it_did: Tested whether including missingness indicators as model features improves clinical prediction, and found it helps in many settings and harms under outcome-dependent missingness
sources.comparator: Models with and without missingness indicators
sources.bearing: Supports, and complicates. Modelling the measurement process is a legitimate design choice with a known failure mode, which is the register this paper argues in

sources.title: Missing data should be handled differently for prediction than for description or causal explanation
sources.notes: 125:183-187. The methodological licence for the whole design: for prediction, unlike causal explanation, the measurement process is admissible information.
sources.what_it_did: Argued that missing data in prediction differs from missing data in causal inference, and that for prediction the measurement process is legitimately usable information
sources.comparator: Not applicable
sources.bearing: Supports, and is the paper's licence. An acquisition-context arm is not a trick; it is admissible information that current benchmarks decline to measure

sources.title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
sources.notes: 14(7):2213. The only located deterioration model that names informative presence: discrimination fell from 0.918 to 0.827 when the informative default was imputed away. Vendor-authored, and flagged as such rather than weighted equally.
sources.what_it_did: Named informative presence inside a clinical deterioration model and measured what imputing the informative default away costs
sources.comparator: The same model with and without the informative default
sources.bearing: Supports, with a conflict caveat. The closest thing to this audit inside a deterioration model, arrived at incidentally

sources.title: Exploring the impact of missingness on racial disparities in predictive performance of a machine learning model for emergency department triage
sources.notes: 6(4):ooad107. A c-statistic gap of roughly 0.03 to 0.06 between a record as it stands at triage and the same record at discharge.
sources.what_it_did: Quantified how much a triage prediction model's discrimination depends on when in the encounter the record is read
sources.comparator: The same features at two points in the encounter
sources.bearing: Supports, in the setting this audit works in: when in an encounter the record is read carries discrimination.

sources.title: Sources of Variation in Cardiovascular Care Cascades
sources.notes: 7(4):e260491. PMID 41931286. 16,475 adults with a troponin test after an emergency visit, restricted to above-median ECG-derived ischaemia risk; the ECG is the restriction variable, not the outcome. Ordering differed by insurance, primary language and sex, while completion exceeded three quarters once a service was scheduled with no group differences. Corrected at this stage: the entry previously described this as a decomposition of variation in ECG use, which it is not, and the related-work sentence written from that description was wrong with it.
sources.what_it_did: Followed coronary artery disease testing and cardiology referral after an emergency-department visit through ordering, scheduling and completion, and located the variation at the ordering step, predicted by insurance, language and sex
sources.comparator: Not applicable; a study of the care decision itself
sources.bearing: Supports the premise one modality downstream. It shows that a care decision in this setting is systematic, patient-linked and concentrated at the order rather than at completion. It measures a referral rather than the ECG, so it does not evidence variation in ECG recording directly, and the manuscript no longer says it does

sources.title: The Risks of Risk Assessment: Causal Blind Spots When Using Prediction Models for Treatment Decisions
sources.notes: 178(9):1326-1333. Fifteen authors including Sperrin and Didelez.
sources.what_it_did: Set out how prediction models should handle features that encode a clinician's action rather than a patient state, and argued reporting guidance should extend over them
sources.comparator: Not applicable
sources.bearing: Supports the recommendation, and shows the reporting argument is already being made in a general journal for a neighbouring class of feature

sources.title: Risk stratification of chest pain in the emergency department using artificial intelligence applied to electrocardiograms
sources.notes: 12(2):e003343. PMID 40889954; full text read at PMC12406858. In external validation the four arms were the ECG-plus-clinical model, a biomarker model, an ECG model and an age-and-sex model, in that order of discrimination.
sources.what_it_did: Reported four nested arms on one emergency-department chest-pain cohort against one composite endpoint, including an explicit age-and-sex-only arm
sources.setting: Emergency department chest pain, 12-lead ECG, 7-day composite
sources.comparator: Yes: age and sex alone, plus a biomarker arm and an ECG-only arm, all on the same cohort and endpoint
sources.bearing: Supports the recommendation and is the precedent it needed. It also complicates the framing usefully, since there the waveform arm does add over the non-signal arms

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Electrocardiography and Health Records to Predict Cardiac Arrest
sources.notes: 5(6 Pt 2):102787. PMID 42114451. Three arms on one cohort, with the health-record-only arm above the ECG-only arm and every pairwise comparison significant after Bonferroni. The design is case-control with matching on age and sex, quoted from the abstract, so neither arm can discriminate on age or sex and the comparison is about what remains once both are held fixed. Recorded at this stage after the design was checked; the entry previously gave the result without the design, and the related-work sentence written from it inherited the omission.
sources.what_it_did: Compared an AI-ECG arm, a health-record arm and their combination for cardiac arrest prediction, and found the health-record arm beat the ECG arm
sources.setting: 12-lead ECG plus EHR, out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, case-control matched on age and sex
sources.comparator: Yes: a health-record-only arm, which won
sources.bearing: Supports strongly, as the cleanest published case of the non-waveform arm beating the waveform arm on the same cohort.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Serial Electrocardiograms for Prediction of All-Cause Mortality in Secondary Care Settings
sources.notes: 5(7):102875. Emergency-department and inpatient adults over fifty; the abstract states that adding clinical variables beyond age and sex did not improve performance.
sources.what_it_did: Used serial AI-ECGs to predict one-year all-cause mortality in acute-care settings and reported that clinical variables beyond age and sex added nothing
sources.setting: 12-lead ECG, emergency department and inpatient, one-year mortality
sources.comparator: Yes: age and sex, and clinical variables beyond them
sources.bearing: Supports the size of the demographic share, and complicates the target. Acquisition-context features are not the clinical variables that were inert here

sources.title: Prediction of mortality from 12-lead electrocardiogram voltage data using a deep neural network
sources.notes: 26(6):886-891. The rhetorical core is that discrimination persists within the subset whose ECGs a physician read as normal.
sources.what_it_did: Predicted one-year mortality from 12-lead voltage data in a large health-system cohort, and reported that discrimination persisted among ECGs read as normal by a physician
sources.setting: 12-lead ECG, one health system, one-year mortality
sources.comparator: None reported; no non-waveform arm
sources.bearing: The founding claim this audit is about. Its normal-ECG argument has a competing reading: which patients receive an ECG read as normal, and when, is itself informative

sources.title: Deep neural network-estimated electrocardiographic age as a mortality predictor
sources.notes: 12(1):5117. The ECG-age gap predicted mortality in both directions and persisted for apparently normal ECGs, replicated in two further cohorts.
sources.what_it_did: Estimated an ECG age from the waveform and showed the gap against chronological age predicts mortality, including for apparently normal ECGs
sources.comparator: Chronological age, as the reference the gap is defined against
sources.bearing: Supports the non-specificity argument most directly. If the prognostic content is largely an ageing signal, a variable known before the waveform exists is part of the mechanism rather than a nuisance

sources.title: Deep Learning for ECG Analysis: Benchmarks and Insights from PTB-XL
sources.venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.notes: 25(5):1519-1528. The reference benchmarking protocol for PTB-XL, whose conventions the audited benchmark inherits; the same senior author.
sources.what_it_did: Established the reference benchmarking protocol for PTB-XL across statement-prediction tasks and, separately, age and sex prediction from the waveform
sources.comparator: Task-specific supervised baselines; no non-signal arm
sources.bearing: Supports the description of the evaluation culture, and makes the point sideways: this literature treats age and sex as things the waveform predicts

sources.title: ECG-FM: an open electrocardiogram foundation model
sources.notes: 8(5):ooaf122. Its released benchmark runs on MIMIC-IV-ECG, the same source database as the audited benchmark.
sources.what_it_did: Released an open ECG foundation model with a benchmark on MIMIC-IV-ECG and reported gains over task-specific supervised baselines in small and medium data regimes
sources.comparator: Task-specific supervised baselines; no non-signal arm
sources.bearing: Supports the description of the evaluation culture and is the closest published methodological neighbour. Even an openly benchmarked foundation model reports no non-signal arm

sources.title: The Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence-Based Models Applied to 12-Lead Electrocardiograms for the Diagnosis of Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review
sources.venue: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians Open (JACEP Open)
sources.notes: 6(5):100240. PROBAST-appraised. Of 24 included studies, one compared against the clinical alternative as it exists in real time and three released code.
sources.what_it_did: Systematically reviewed AI applied to 12-lead ECGs for acute coronary syndrome in suspected-ACS adults, appraised with PROBAST, and recorded what each study compared against
sources.setting: 12-lead ECG, emergency department, acute coronary syndrome
sources.comparator: Clinician ECG interpretation, in a minority of studies
sources.bearing: Supports the diagnosis of the comparison culture, quantified and specific to the emergency department. Its comparator is a clinician rather than a model arm

sources.title: Artificial intelligence in electrocardiogram-based prediction of heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.notes: 12:1659298. PROSPERO CRD420251012231. The AI-ECG pooled estimate and the traditional model's estimate did not differ significantly. Five studies, high heterogeneity, and the comparison is indirect rather than within-cohort; both cautions belong wherever this is cited.
sources.what_it_did: Pooled AI-ECG heart-failure prediction across eleven cohorts and compared the pooled estimate against a conventional risk model, finding no significant difference
sources.comparator: Yes: a traditional risk model, indirectly compared
sources.bearing: Supports the central claim with a pooled estimate, subject to indirectness and heterogeneity

sources.title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
sources.notes: 385:e078378. Full-text XML read in-session: the checklist contains no occurrence of baseline, comparator, benchmark, reference model or simpler model. Its only comparator hook, item 12e, is conditional on model comparison being relevant. Items 18c and 18d require protocol access and registration information. Crossref records a correction at 10.1136/bmj.q902. Note that 10.1136/bmj.q824 is a different item, an editorial that surfaces first on a naive search for this guideline and is not it.
sources.what_it_did: Updated the reporting guidance for clinical prediction model studies to cover regression and machine learning methods
sources.comparator: Conditional only; no required comparator arm
sources.bearing: Both the anchor and the gap. It supports the paper's pre-registration practice directly, and its silence on a required comparator is the opening the recommendation fills

sources.title: PROBAST+AI: an updated quality, risk of bias, and applicability assessment tool for prediction models using regression or artificial intelligence methods
sources.notes: 388:e082505. A comparator model is named once, inside the PICOTS scoping step, and is not a scored signalling question. Signalling question 2.4 asks whether the predictors were available at the moment the model was intended to be used.
sources.what_it_did: Updated the risk-of-bias and applicability tool for prediction models using regression or AI, separating model development from model evaluation
sources.comparator: Named in scoping, not scored
sources.bearing: Supports on two counts. A comparator model is already a first-class scoping element, and its availability question is the nearest thing in any tool to this paper's objection

sources.title: Minimum information about clinical artificial intelligence modeling: the MI-CLAIM checklist
sources.notes: 26(9):1320-1324. Published as a Comment rather than as a Delphi-consensus guideline, which is worth stating if a reviewer presses. Part 1 requires identifying the current clinical baseline; Part 4 requires a results table carrying the baseline and the new model together.
sources.what_it_did: Set a minimum reporting standard for clinical AI modelling that makes a named baseline arm a requirement rather than a conditional
sources.comparator: Required: the current clinical baseline, in the same results table
sources.bearing: Supports the recommendation and is the closest existing peg. Its baseline is the standard of care; this paper argues the set should also include what the acquisition context alone achieves

sources.title: Reporting Recommendations for Tumor Marker Prognostic Studies (REMARK): explanation and elaboration
sources.notes: 9(5):e1001216. Checklist items were extracted from the publisher's manuscript XML after two fetches of the same paper returned contradictory item numbering; the numbering used here is the one the XML supports. Item 17 requires the marker to be reported alongside standard prognostic variables regardless of statistical significance.
sources.what_it_did: Set reporting recommendations for tumour marker prognostic studies, including a specified minimum set of standard prognostic variables and a requirement to report them regardless of significance
sources.comparator: Required: standard prognostic variables, reported whether or not significant
sources.bearing: Supports the recommendation on two axes at once, and is the clearest precedent for a guideline that both names a minimum comparator and forbids suppressing it when it disappoints

sources.title: Consolidated Reporting Guidelines for Prognostic and Diagnostic Machine Learning Modeling Studies: Development and Validation
sources.notes: 25:e48763. Item 1.9 requires existing model performance benchmarks and a justification for why a traditional statistical model would not suffice. The frequently cited companion editorial in the same journal is not the guideline.
sources.what_it_did: Consolidated reporting guidelines for prognostic and diagnostic machine-learning studies, requiring a benchmark for comparison and a justification against a simpler model
sources.comparator: Required: an existing performance benchmark, with a justification against a simpler model
sources.bearing: Supports the recommendation from the venue's own readership. The paper's recommendation is a specific answer to the question this guideline already asks

authors: on behalf of Topic Group "Evaluating diagnostic tests and prediction models" of the STRATOS initiative
sources.title: Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics
sources.notes: 17(1):230. Argues that calibration receives little attention relative to discrimination and that poorly calibrated algorithms can mislead clinical decisions.
sources.what_it_did: Argued that calibration is systematically neglected relative to discrimination and set out how to assess and report it
sources.comparator: Not applicable
sources.bearing: Adopted. A paper arguing that a discrimination number can be produced by something other than the signal it is credited to is the paper that should not report discrimination alone

sources.title: A simple, step-by-step guide to interpreting decision curve analysis
sources.notes: 3:18. A didactic reading of a decision curve from the method's own author, thirteen years after [vickers2006], written because the interpretation was widely misunderstood.
sources.what_it_did: Gave a step-by-step interpretive standard for decision curve analysis and stated the decision rule for recommending a model
sources.comparator: Treat-all and treat-none
sources.bearing: Adopted, and fixes the thinnest methodological citation in the manuscript, which previously rested on the 2006 paper alone

sources.title: Almost all articles on cancer prognostic markers report statistically significant results
sources.notes: 43(17):2559-2579. Over nine in ten prognostic-marker articles in both examined databases reported positive findings, and fully negative abstracts were rare.
sources.what_it_did: Measured how often prognostic-marker articles report statistically significant results and found the overwhelming majority positive
sources.comparator: Not applicable
sources.bearing: Makes this paper's four reported failures structurally interesting rather than merely disappointing, by establishing how rare a published negative prognostic result is

sources.title: CLIC: Contextual Language-Informed Cardiac Pathology Classification
sources.venue: arXiv (ICLR 2026 Workshop on Time Series in the Age of Large Models)
sources.notes: arXiv:2605.19132v1 [cs.LG], submitted 2026-05-18, 6 pages, accepted at the ICLR 2026 TSALM workshop. Unreviewed in the sense this protocol uses: a workshop acceptance is not a journal or main-conference review, and the archival version is the preprint. Located by the re-run search of 2026-09-13 and named in the second external review; the 2026-09-06 search did not reach it, which is the coverage gap that review reports.
sources.what_it_did: Encoded patient demographics and ECG acquisition metadata as natural-language text alongside the signal, and showed that template-based contextual descriptions improve downstream cardiac pathology classification over signal-only models
sources.comparator: None of the kind this audit asks for: context is an ADDED input, never fitted alone, and no context-only arm is reported
sources.bearing: Supports the premise and not the claim. It is the nearest 2026 work on ECG acquisition context and establishes independently that the variables matter, but it uses them to improve a diagnostic classifier rather than to bound one, and its outcome is a pathology label rather than a prognostic horizon.

sources.title: Position: Evaluation of ECG Representations Must Be Fixed
sources.notes: arXiv:2602.17531v2 [cs.LG], submitted 2026-02-19 and revised 2026-05-29. Unreviewed: no venue is claimed. Located by the re-run search of 2026-09-13; neither external review names it, and it is the closer precedent of the two the second review asked for.
sources.what_it_did: Argued that 12-lead ECG representation benchmarking is converged on three diagnostic multi-label datasets and evaluated with the wrong protocol, and showed empirically across five pre-training approaches and six settings that a RANDOMLY INITIALISED encoder with linear evaluation matches state-of-the-art pre-training on many tasks
sources.comparator: A trivial signal baseline, the random encoder, argued for as a standing requirement. Not a non-signal arm
sources.bearing: Supports the recommendation from the other side. It reaches the same structural conclusion, that ECG benchmarks report headline numbers without the cheap baseline that would bound them, by withholding training rather than by withholding the waveform. Independent, contemporaneous, and about the field this audit addresses.

_p8_note: Extended at this stage under the project's design notes. Every entry carries four synthesis fields beyond the bibliographic ones: what_it_did, setting, comparator and bearing. `comparator` is the field the review exists for, because the manuscript's positive claim is that a non-signal comparator arm is missing from this literature, and a reader has to be able to check that source by source. scripts/make_related_work_table.py renders the related-work summary table from these fields, so the table cannot drift from the log.
